decisions.choice: son of man: human being, a mortal standing before God
decisions.reason: "Son of" in Hebrew can mean "one belonging to the class of", so "son of man" means simply a human being, one of humankind, as in Psalm 8:5 ("what is man ... and the son of man") and Numbers 23:19. God addresses Ezekiel this way about ninety-three times, and never by his name. Set beside the glory of chapter 1, the phrase stresses that Ezekiel is a mortal creature before God, and also that God has chosen to speak to a human being. It is not the title "the Son of Man" that Jesus uses of himself in the Gospels, which takes up the "one like a son of man" of Daniel 7:13; there it names a figure in a vision, while here it is God's way of addressing the prophet.

decisions.choice: stand on your feet: get up from the ground
decisions.reason: Ezekiel has fallen on his face before the glory (1:28). The first word God speaks to him is a command to stand, so that he can be spoken to and sent, as Daniel is raised to his feet in Daniel 10:11. The speaker is the one on the throne, whose voice was heard at the end of chapter 1.

decisions.choice: son of man, at every level, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The founder's ruling keeps "son of man" at every level, Readable included, so that the reader meets the same words each time God addresses Ezekiel. The phrase refers to one specific man, so it takes no gender setting. Later uses in the book refer back to this note.

decisions.choice: He (B, R): a pronoun for God
decisions.reason: The speaker is the LORD (1:28; 2:4). At the start of a sentence the pronoun is capitalized under either setting. Readable says "I want to speak with you" for the sense of "so that I may speak with you".

decisions.choice: "hijo de hombre", lowercase except at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: Book-wide: God's address to Ezekiel means "mortal, human being"; Spanish keeps "hijo de hombre" at every level, as Revelation 1:13 "un hijo de hombre", and never the Gospels' title "Hijo del Hombre"; no gender span, since Ezekiel is one man

decisions.choice: "me dijo", with no subject pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so the English "He" has no free pronoun to carry a deity_pronoun span here

decisions.choice: Hỡi con người, lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: "Con người" is the ordinary Vietnamese for "human being", which is what the Hebrew means, so the sense comes through with no gloss. It is never capitalised and takes no span: capitalised "Con Người" is kept for Jesus' title in the Gospels (Matthew 24:30), and this is not that title. Every later "son of man" in Ezekiel refers back here.

decisions.choice: ngươi (L); con (B, R)
decisions.reason: God speaks to his prophet as to one person under his care: "ngươi" at Literal, "con" at Balanced and Readable, as he speaks to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:5-19). Ezekiel calls himself "tôi" in the narrative and "con" when he speaks to God. This holds through the book.

decisions.choice: "사람의 아들아" at every level, with no gender span
decisions.reason: God's address to Ezekiel means "human being, mortal"; "인자" is Jesus's title in the Korean New Testament, so Ezekiel keeps a plain wording that is not the Gospel title. Later uses in the book refer back to this decision.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Ezekiel in 해라체 with "너" ("서라"), and the narration gives God the honorific ("그분께서 … 말씀하셨다")
decisions.reason: The speech levels set for the prophets: God speaks in the plain style and never takes -시- in his own mouth; Ezekiel's first-person narration honours him.

decisions.choice: "fils d'homme", lowercase and with no article, at every level, Readable included, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The phrase means a human being, a mortal before God (the English meaning decision). French keeps it at every level, as the English does, but never in the form "le Fils de l'homme", which is Jesus's title in the Gospels; with no article and a lowercase f it reads as an address to a man, not as the title. Ezekiel is one man, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: God says "tu" to Ezekiel
decisions.reason: One person is addressed in the singular, as everywhere in the French translation; the term sheet fixes "tu" from God to the prophet.

decisions.choice: mwana wa binadamu, lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: God's address to Ezekiel means "human being", a mortal before God (meaning decision). Swahili keeps the phrase at every level, as the English keeps "son of man", but words it "mwana wa binadamu" with a small letter, so that it is not read as Jesus' title "Mwana wa Adamu" in the Gospels. "Mwanadamu", the everyday word for a human being, would be plainer at Readable.

decisions.choice: Filho do homem / filho do homem (every level), no gender setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book (ben-adam, 93 times): God's name for Ezekiel (m1) is "filho do homem" at every level, Readable included, as the English keeps "son of man" (r-en-1), so that the reader meets the same words each time. It is written with a capital only at the start of a sentence; the lowercase "homem" keeps it apart from the Gospels' title "o Filho do Homem" (style section 6), which takes capitals. It names one man, so it takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: tu (God to Ezekiel): fica, levanta-te, contigo
decisions.reason: For the whole book: God speaks to Ezekiel with "tu" at every level, as he speaks to one person through the Old Testament and to Isaiah and Jeremiah, and Ezekiel answers him with "tu" (4:14; 9:8; 11:13). God's words to the house of Israel or the elders as a group take "vocês"; people speak to Ezekiel with "você".

source.text: וַתָּ֧בֹא בִ֣י ר֗וּחַ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י וַתַּעֲמִדֵ֖נִי עַל־רַגְלָ֑י וָאֶשְׁמַ֕ע אֵ֖ת מִדַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלָֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came into me a spirit when he spoke to me, and it made me stand on my feet, and I heard [one] speaking to me.

sw.L: Na Roho akaingia ndani yangu alipokuwa akisema nami, akanisimamisha kwa miguu yangu, nami nikamsikia akisema nami.

es.L: Y entró en mí el Espíritu cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me hablaba, y me hizo poner sobre mis pies, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oí hablándome.
es.B: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me hablaba, el Espíritu entró en mí y me puso en pie, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oí que me hablaba.

vi.L: Và Thần Linh đã vào trong tôi khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với tôi, và [Thần Linh] làm cho tôi đứng trên chân mình, và tôi nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang phán với tôi.
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với tôi, Thần Linh vào trong tôi và làm cho tôi đứng dậy trên chân mình, và tôi nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang phán với tôi.
vi.R: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang phán, Thần Linh vào trong tôi và làm cho tôi đứng dậy. Rồi tôi nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với tôi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 나에게 말씀하실 때에 영이 내 속에 들어와 나를 내 발로 서게 하셨고, 나는 나에게 말씀하시는 분의 [소리를] 들었다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나에게 말씀하실 때에 영이 내 속에 들어와 나를 일으켜 세우셨다. 그리고 나는 그분께서 나에게 말씀하시는 소리를 들었다.
ko.R: 그분께서 말씀하실 때에 영이 내 속에 들어와 나를 일으켜 세우셨다. 그리고 그분께서 나에게 말씀하시는 소리가 들렸다.

fr.L: Et [l’]Esprit entra en moi pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me parlait, et il me fit tenir sur mes pieds, et je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendis qui me parlait.
fr.B: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me parlait, l’Esprit entra en moi et me remit debout sur mes pieds, et je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendis qui me parlait.
fr.R: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait, l’Esprit est entré en moi et m’a fait lever. Alors je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai entendu qui me parlait.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the LORD's Spirit, giving Ezekiel the strength to stand
alternatives: a spirit: strength or breath of life
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit, and it has no article here ("a spirit"). What Ezekiel cannot do by himself, the spirit does: it enters him and sets him on his feet, as it does again in 3:24. Ezekiel later calls it "the Spirit of the LORD" (11:5) and "the Spirit of God" (11:24), and the same spirit lifts and carries him (3:12, 14; 8:3). So it is taken as the LORD's own Spirit. It could also be read as the breath of life, strength returning to him, as in 37:5-10.

decisions.choice: as he spoke ... I heard him speaking: the LORD's speech goes on
decisions.reason: The verse sets the scene for the speech that resumes in verse 3. The last verb has no subject; it means "the one speaking", the same voice as in 1:28.

decisions.choice: the Spirit, capitalized (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Isaiah's rule for this word, which Ezekiel follows, capitalizes "Spirit" where it is God's Spirit. It is so taken here (m1), with the uncertainty footnoted, and the same wording is used where the spirit lifts Ezekiel or enters him (3:12, 14, 24). Literal brackets "the", since the Hebrew has no article. Where the word is the force that moves the living creatures (1:12, 20), the text does not say whose spirit it is, and it stays lowercase.

decisions.choice: Roho, capitalized, with personal agreement
decisions.reason: The English reads this as the LORD's Spirit (meaning decision), so Swahili writes "Roho" with a capital, as the terms note sets it, and gives it the personal agreement of the published New Testament ("Roho aliingia"). The pronouns for God here are inside the verbs ("alipokuwa", "nikamsikia"), so there is no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: Thần Linh, capitalised
decisions.reason: The LORD's Spirit, as Isaiah 44:3 and 61:1 publish it. The Old Testament keeps "Thần Linh"; "Thánh Linh" is the New Testament's word.

decisions.choice: "영" with the honorific ("세우셨다")
decisions.reason: God's Spirit in the prophets is "영" and takes -시-, as in the published Isaiah; "성령" stays the New Testament word.

decisions.choice: "je {{deity_pronoun:l'|L'}}entendis qui me parlait": the span on the elided object pronoun
decisions.reason: French makes the speaker the object of "entendre", so the deity_pronoun span the English puts on "him" sits on the elided "l'".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־גּוֹיִ֥ם הַמּוֹרְדִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָרְדוּ־בִ֑י הֵ֤מָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם֙ פָּ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֔י עַד־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, sending I you to [the] sons of Israel, to nations the rebellious who have rebelled against me; they and their fathers have transgressed against me until [the] bone of the day this.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to rebellious nations that rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; they and their fathers have transgressed against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to this very day.
en.B: He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, to rebellious nations that have revolted against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They and their ancestors have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to this very day.
en.R: He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They are nations that have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They and their ancestors have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, right up to this day.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, eu te envio aos filhos de Israel, a nações rebeldes que se rebelaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}; eles e os seus pais transgrediram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} até este mesmo dia.
pt.B: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, eu te envio aos israelitas, a nações rebeldes que se revoltaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Eles e os seus antepassados se rebelaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} até este mesmo dia.
pt.R: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, eu te envio aos israelitas. Eles são nações que se voltaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Eles e os seus antepassados pecaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} até o dia de hoje.

sw.L: Naye akaniambia, "Mwana wa binadamu, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakutuma kwa wana wa Israeli, kwa mataifa yaliyoasi, yaliyoniasi; wao na baba zao wamenikosea hadi siku hii hii.
sw.B: Akaniambia, "Mwana wa binadamu, ninakutuma kwa Waisraeli, kwa mataifa yaliyoasi ambayo yameniasi. Wao na babu zao wameniasi hadi leo hii.
sw.R: Akaniambia, "Mwana wa binadamu, ninakutuma kwa Waisraeli. Wao ni mataifa ambayo yamegeuka kunipinga. Wao na babu zao wamenitendea dhambi mpaka siku hii ya leo.

es.L: Y me dijo: «Hijo de hombre, yo te envío a los hijos de Israel, a naciones rebeldes que se rebelaron contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; ellos y sus padres han transgredido contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} hasta este mismo día.
es.B: Me dijo: «Hijo de hombre, yo te envío a los israelitas, a naciones rebeldes que se han sublevado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Ellos y sus antepasados se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Me dijo: «Hijo de hombre, te envío al pueblo de Israel. Son naciones que se han puesto en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Ellos y sus antepasados han pecado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} hasta el día de hoy.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với tôi: "Hỡi con người, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang sai ngươi đến cùng con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên, đến cùng các dân tộc phản nghịch đã nổi loạn chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; chúng và tổ phụ chúng đã phạm tội nghịch cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho đến chính ngày nay.
vi.B: Ngài phán với tôi: "Hỡi con người, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai con đến với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, đến với những dân tộc phản nghịch đã nổi lên chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Chúng và tổ tiên chúng đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho đến tận ngày nay.
vi.R: Ngài phán với tôi: "Hỡi con người, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai con đến với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Chúng là những dân tộc đã chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Chúng và tổ tiên chúng đã phạm tội với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho đến tận hôm nay.

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "사람의 아들아, 내가 너를 이스라엘 자손에게, 나를 거역한 거역하는 민족들에게 보낸다. 그들과 그들의 조상들은 바로 이날까지 나에게 반역했다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "사람의 아들아, 내가 너를 이스라엘 백성에게, 곧 나를 거역한 반역하는 민족들에게 보낸다. 그들과 그들의 조상들은 바로 오늘까지 나에게 반역해 왔다.
ko.R: 그분께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "사람의 아들아, 내가 너를 이스라엘 사람들에게 보낸다. 그들은 나에게 등을 돌린 민족들이다. 그들과 그들의 조상들은 오늘까지 줄곧 나에게 죄를 지었다.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me dit : « Fils d’homme, je t’envoie vers les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, vers des nations rebelles qui se sont rebellées contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; eux et leurs pères ont commis des transgressions contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} jusqu’à ce jour même.
fr.B: Il me dit : « Fils d’homme, je t’envoie vers les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, vers des nations rebelles qui se sont révoltées contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Eux et leurs ancêtres se sont rebellés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} jusqu’à ce jour même.
fr.R: Il m’a dit : « Fils d’homme, je t’envoie vers les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Ce sont des nations qui se sont tournées contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Eux et leurs ancêtres ont péché contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} jusqu’à aujourd’hui.

decisions.choice: rebellious nations: Israel has become like the nations
decisions.reason: The word for "nations" is normally used for the peoples other than Israel. Using it of Israel, and in the plural, puts God's own people on a level with the nations that do not know him. It may also have the two kingdoms in mind, Israel and Judah, whose history of revolt chapters 16, 20 and 23 retell.

decisions.choice: to the bone of this day: to this very day
decisions.reason: "The bone of the day" means the day itself, this very day. The rebellion did not stop with the ancestors; it goes on in the people Ezekiel is sent to.

decisions.choice: I am sending you: the prophet's commission
decisions.reason: The LORD sends Ezekiel as he sent Moses (Exodus 3:10), Isaiah (Isaiah 6:8) and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:7). The commission runs from here to 3:11.

decisions.choice: rebelled ... transgressed (L); revolted ... rebelled (B); turned against ... sinned (R)
decisions.reason: The verb for "transgress" is "transgress" / "rebel" / "sin" in the prophets. Since Balanced uses "rebel" for it, it says "revolted" for the first verb, which also means to rebel. Literal keeps "the sons of Israel" and "fathers"; Balanced and Readable say "Israelites" through the gender setting, and "ancestors". The open quotation mark begins the LORD's charge to Ezekiel, which runs to the end of verse 8.

decisions.choice: wana wa Israeli (L); Waisraeli (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: wana wa Israeli at every level
decisions.reason: The English offers "Israelites" / "sons of Israel" through the gender setting. Swahili "Waisraeli" names the whole people and Literal keeps the Hebrew "wana wa Israeli", as the published books do, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B); "el pueblo de Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide; these already include women, so no gender span

decisions.choice: "han transgredido" (L); "se han rebelado" (B); "han pecado" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide levels for pasha (transgress)

decisions.choice: con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên (L); dân Y-sơ-ra-ên (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "Israelites / sons of Israel" as a setting. "Con cái" and "dân" already include men and women, so Vietnamese has no second wording to offer.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L); "이스라엘 백성" (B); "이스라엘 사람들" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Korean words already include women and men, so the English gender span has no Korean counterpart; the three levels follow the Pentateuch wording.

decisions.choice: "반역하다" (L, B); "죄를 짓다" (R) for the verb of transgression; "거역하다" for the verb of rebellion
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the transgression verb; the rebellion verb takes another word so that Literal keeps the two Hebrew verbs apart.

decisions.choice: "les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d'Israël" (Literal); "les {{gender:Israélites|fils d'Israël}}" (Balanced, Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, as the Pentateuch: the people as a whole, men and women, with the traditional wording as the alternative.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the Old Testament terms set it: Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters and "os israelitas" is inclusive, so neither needs the gender setting the English uses at Balanced and Readable. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, Balanced and Readable the name of the people.

source.text: וְהַבָּנִ֗ים קְשֵׁ֤י פָנִים֙ וְחִזְקֵי־לֵ֔ב אֲנִ֛י שׁוֹלֵ֥חַ אוֹתְךָ֖ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the sons [are] hard of face and strong of heart; I [am] sending you to them, and you will say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And {{gender:the children|the sons}} [are] hard of face and stubborn of heart; I am sending you to them, and you will say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Their descendants are brazen and stubborn. I am sending you to them, and you will say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this.
en.R: Their descendants are shameless and stubborn. I am sending you to them, and you must tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says.

pt.L: E os filhos [são] duros de rosto e obstinados de coração; eu te envio a eles, e tu lhes dirás: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.B: Os seus descendentes são descarados e obstinados. Eu te envio a eles, e tu lhes dirás: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.R: Os descendentes deles não têm vergonha e são teimosos. Eu te envio a eles, e tu tens de lhes dizer: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz.

sw.L: Na wana hao [ni] wagumu wa uso na wakaidi wa moyo; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakutuma kwao, nawe utawaambia, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asema hivi.
sw.B: Wazao wao hawana haya na ni wakaidi. Ninakutuma kwao, nawe utawaambia, Hivi ndivyo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asemavyo.
sw.R: Wazao wao hawaoni aibu, tena ni wakaidi. Ninakutuma kwao, nawe ni lazima uwaambie, Hili ndilo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} analosema.

es.L: Y los hijos [son] duros de rostro y obstinados de corazón; yo te envío a ellos, y les dirás: Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Sus descendientes son descarados y obstinados. Yo te envío a ellos, y les dirás: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto.
es.R: Sus descendientes no tienen vergüenza y son tercos. Te envío a ellos, y tienes que decirles: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Và con cái [ấy] mặt dày và lòng cứng cỏi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang sai ngươi đến cùng chúng, và ngươi sẽ nói với chúng: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này.
vi.B: Con cháu chúng trơ tráo và cứng lòng. Ta sai con đến với chúng, và con sẽ nói với chúng: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy.
vi.R: Con cháu chúng không biết xấu hổ và rất cứng đầu. Ta sai con đến với chúng, và con phải nói với chúng: Đây là lời Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 그리고 그 자손들은 얼굴이 굳고 마음이 완고하다. 내가 너를 그들에게 보내니, 너는 그들에게 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다.
ko.B: 그들의 자손들은 뻔뻔하고 고집이 세다. 내가 너를 그들에게 보낸다. 너는 그들에게 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다.
ko.R: 그들의 자손들은 부끄러운 줄 모르고 고집이 세다. 내가 너를 그들에게 보낸다. 너는 그들에게 이렇게 전해야 한다. 이것은 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} [sont] durs de visage et obstinés de cœur ; je t’envoie vers eux, et tu leur diras : Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Leurs descendants ont le front dur et le cœur obstiné. Je t’envoie vers eux, et tu leur diras : Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci.
fr.R: Leurs descendants sont effrontés et têtus. Je t’envoie vers eux, et tu devras leur dire : Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: hard of face and stubborn of heart: shameless and obstinate
decisions.reason: A hard face is a brazen one that does not blush or give way (Jeremiah 5:3; Proverbs 21:29); a strong heart is a will set against God. The two phrases come back in 3:7-9, where God makes Ezekiel's face and forehead as hard as theirs.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD: the message is the LORD's own
decisions.reason: The verse gives the formula and nothing after it. What matters at this point is not the content of the message but whose it is: Ezekiel is to speak as a messenger with the LORD's authority, not in his own name. The formula, with the title "the Lord GOD", is Ezekiel's usual way of introducing the LORD's words.

decisions.choice: the children: the present generation, set against the fathers
decisions.reason: Verse 3 speaks of "they and their fathers"; here the word for sons means the people now living, the children of those ancestors.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The prophets' formula, as set for Isaiah and Jeremiah, with "the Lord GOD" for the Lord with the divine name. The message Ezekiel is to deliver takes no quotation marks of its own, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: Bwana MUNGU asema hivi (L); Hivi ndivyo Bwana MUNGU asemavyo (B); Hili ndilo Bwana MUNGU analosema (R)
decisions.reason: The formula returns about 120 times in Ezekiel and keeps this wording at each level, as the terms note sets it. Adonai YHWH is "Bwana" followed by MUNGU in capitals, with the divine_name span on MUNGU only, as the published Jeremiah 1:6.

decisions.choice: "Así dice el Señor DIOS" (L); "El Señor DIOS dice esto" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el Señor DIOS" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide formula, as Isaiah and Jeremiah in Spanish; the message Ezekiel is to deliver takes no quotation marks

decisions.choice: "los hijos", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters

decisions.choice: Chúa là CHÚA phán thế này (L); Chúa là CHÚA phán như vầy (B); Đây là lời Chúa là CHÚA phán (R)
decisions.reason: "The Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH) is "Chúa là CHÚA" at every level, as Isaiah 28:16: "Chúa" plain, the divine name in its span. The formula takes a colon and no quotation marks, since the message Ezekiel is told to give is the LORD's own. "Declares the Lord GOD" is "Chúa là CHÚA phán vậy" (L, B) / "Chúa là CHÚA phán" (R). These hold for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "$LG께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L); "…이렇게 말씀하신다" (B); "…께서 하시는 말씀이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as published in Isaiah and Jeremiah, ending in a period; it keeps "께서" even in God's mouth. After the span 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, only particles that fit both 하나님 and 야훼 are used (께서, 께, 의, 도, 만, 에게, 인, 이다), here and through the book.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le Seigneur DIEU :" (Literal); "Le Seigneur DIEU dit ceci :" (Balanced); "Voici ce que dit le Seigneur DIEU :" (Readable), for the whole book, with no quotation marks around the message
decisions.reason: The formula as published in Kings, Isaiah and Jeremiah; Adonai YHWH is "le Seigneur" with the divine name span on "DIEU" alone. The message the prophet is told to deliver takes no quotation marks, as the term sheet says.

decisions.choice: Assim diz o Senhor DEUS (L, B); É isto que o Senhor DEUS diz (R); declara o Senhor DEUS (L, B), diz o Senhor DEUS (R) for ne'um
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Ezekiel's messenger formula, with Adonai and the divine name (m2), takes the wording Isaiah 7:7 and 28:16 set in Portuguese, "Assim diz o Senhor DEUS" at Literal and Balanced and "É isto que o Senhor DEUS diz" at Readable; the English Balanced's "The Lord GOD says this" has no better Portuguese than the familiar formula. Ne'um, the formula that seals a word as God's (5:11 and after), is "declara o Senhor DEUS" at Literal and Balanced and "diz o Senhor DEUS" at Readable, as Isaiah 1:24 and Jeremiah 1:8. "Senhor DEUS" keeps the default from reading "Senhor SENHOR". The message takes no quotation marks of its own, as in the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: os filhos, no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "the children" under the gender setting. Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters, so Literal says "os filhos" with no setting; Balanced and Readable say "descendentes", as the English does (m3).

source.text: וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ אִם־יִשְׁמְע֣וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּ֔לוּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵ֑מָּה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they, whether they will hear or whether they will refrain, for a house of rebellion [are] they, and they will know that a prophet has been in their midst.

en.L: And they, whether they hear or refrain—for they [are] a house of rebellion—they will know that a prophet has been among them.
en.B: Whether they listen or refuse—for they are a rebellious house—they will come to know that a prophet has been among them.
en.R: They are people who refuse to obey. But whether they listen or not, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

pt.L: E eles, quer ouçam, quer deixem de ouvir — pois eles [são] uma casa de rebelião —, saberão que um profeta esteve no meio deles.
pt.B: Quer escutem, quer se recusem — pois são uma casa rebelde —, eles saberão que um profeta esteve no meio deles.
pt.R: Eles são um povo que se recusa a obedecer. Mas, quer escutem, quer não, eles saberão que um profeta esteve no meio deles.

sw.L: Nao, kwamba watasikia au kwamba wataacha, kwa maana wao [ni] nyumba ya uasi, watajua kwamba nabii amekuwa katikati yao.
sw.B: Kwamba watasikiliza au watakataa, kwa maana wao ni nyumba ya waasi, watatambua kwamba nabii amekuwa kati yao.
sw.R: Wao ni watu wanaokataa kutii. Lakini kwamba watasikiliza au hawatasikiliza, watajua kwamba nabii amekuwa kati yao.

es.L: Y ellos, ya sea que escuchen o que dejen de escuchar —porque ellos [son] una casa de rebelión—, sabrán que ha habido un profeta en medio de ellos.
es.B: Ya sea que escuchen o que se nieguen —porque son una casa rebelde—, llegarán a saber que ha habido un profeta entre ellos.
es.R: Son un pueblo que se niega a obedecer. Pero, escuchen o no, sabrán que ha habido un profeta entre ellos.

vi.L: Và chúng, dù chúng nghe hay chúng từ chối, vì chúng [là] nhà của sự phản nghịch, chúng sẽ biết rằng đã có một nhà tiên tri ở giữa chúng.
vi.B: Dù chúng nghe hay không chịu nghe, vì chúng là nhà phản nghịch, chúng sẽ biết rằng đã có một nhà tiên tri ở giữa chúng.
vi.R: Chúng là dân không chịu vâng lời. Nhưng dù chúng có nghe hay không, chúng sẽ biết rằng đã có một nhà tiên tri ở giữa chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은, 듣든지 거부하든지, 그들은 반역의 집이니, 자기들 가운데 예언자가 있었다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 그들이 듣든지 듣기를 거부하든지, 그들은 반역하는 족속이니, 자기들 가운데 예언자가 있었다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 말을 듣지 않는 백성이다. 하지만 그들이 듣든지 듣지 않든지, 자기들 가운데 예언자가 있었다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.

fr.L: Et eux, qu’ils écoutent ou qu’ils s’abstiennent — car ils [sont] une maison de rébellion —, ils sauront qu’un prophète a été au milieu d’eux.
fr.B: Qu’ils écoutent ou qu’ils refusent — car c’est une maison rebelle —, ils sauront qu’un prophète a été parmi eux.
fr.R: C’est un peuple qui refuse d’obéir. Mais qu’ils écoutent ou non, ils sauront qu’un prophète a été parmi eux.

decisions.choice: a house of rebellion: a people defined by rebellion
decisions.reason: The word for rebellion means defiance, a stubborn refusal to obey (Numbers 17:25; Deuteronomy 31:27). "House" is the household or people of Israel, so that "the house of Israel" has become "the house of rebellion", a people whose family likeness is revolt. It is the book's name for the people in Ezekiel's commission (2:5-8; 3:9, 26-27) and comes back in 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3 and 44:6. Later uses refer back to this note.

decisions.choice: whether they hear or refuse: the result does not depend on their answer
decisions.reason: The second verb means to stop, hold back or refrain, and so to refuse. Ezekiel's task is to speak, not to persuade; whatever they do, they will not be able to say that no prophet warned them.

decisions.choice: they will know that a prophet has been among them: the word will prove true
decisions.reason: When the judgment Ezekiel announces comes, the people will know that a true prophet spoke to them. The promise is repeated when Jerusalem falls (33:33), and it goes with the book's refrain "and you will know that I am the LORD" (6:7).

decisions.choice: a house of rebellion (L); a rebellious house (B); people who refuse to obey (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Ezekiel. Readable says what the phrase means, since "house" for a people is not plain English (m1), and puts that sentence first so that "whether they listen or not" can follow it.

decisions.choice: whether they hear or refrain (L); whether they listen or refuse (B); whether they listen or not (R)
decisions.reason: The wording for this phrase each time it returns (2:7; 3:11; compare 3:27).

decisions.choice: nyumba ya uasi (L); nyumba ya waasi (B); watu wanaokataa kutii (R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's name for Israel returns through chapters 2 to 24, and each level keeps this wording, following the three English levels and the terms note.

decisions.choice: "una casa de rebelión" (L); "una casa rebelde" (B); "un pueblo que se niega a obedecer" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide wording for bet meri

decisions.choice: nhà của sự phản nghịch (L); nhà phản nghịch (B); dân không chịu vâng lời (R)
decisions.reason: Bet meri, Ezekiel's name for Israel, kept in one wording per level through the book. "Chúng" is used for Israel under judgment, as in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "반역의 집" (L); "반역하는 족속" (B); "말을 듣지 않는 백성" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the house of rebellion, used through the book; "패역한" is the older Korean Bible word.

decisions.choice: "une maison de rébellion" (Literal); "une maison rebelle" (Balanced); "un peuple qui refuse d'obéir" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's three wordings, matching the English; Balanced keeps "maison" for the people, as French Bibles do for "the house of Israel".

decisions.choice: uma casa de rebelião (L); a casa rebelde (B); um povo que se recusa a obedecer (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (2:5-8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3; 44:6): the phrase (m1) keeps one wording at each level, as the English does (r-en-1). Literal keeps the noun; Balanced says "a casa rebelde", as the shared rules for Ezekiel set it; Readable says what "house" means, a people, and what their rebellion is.

decisions.choice: quer ouçam, quer deixem de ouvir (L); quer escutem, quer se recusem (B); quer escutem, quer não (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the pair returns (2:7; 3:11, 27): one wording at each level, as the English (r-en-2). Literal keeps the sense of the second verb, to hold back (m2), with "deixar de ouvir".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָ֠דָם אַל־תִּירָ֨א מֵהֶ֜ם וּמִדִּבְרֵיהֶ֣ם אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י סָרָבִ֤ים וְסַלּוֹנִים֙ אוֹתָ֔ךְ וְאֶל־עַקְרַבִּ֖ים אַתָּ֣ה יוֹשֵׁ֑ב מִדִּבְרֵיהֶ֤ם אַל־תִּירָא֙ וּמִפְּנֵיהֶ֣ם אַל־תֵּחָ֔ת כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, and of their words do not be afraid, for briers and thorns [are] with you, and to scorpions you [are] sitting; of their words do not be afraid, and at their faces do not be dismayed, for a house of rebellion [are] they.

en.L: And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, and do not be afraid of their words, even though briers and thorns [are] with you and you are sitting among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words, and do not be dismayed at their faces, for they [are] a house of rebellion.
en.B: As for you, son of man, do not fear them or what they say, though thorns and briers surround you and you live among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house.
en.R: But you, son of man, must not be afraid of them or of what they say. They will be like thorns and briers around you, and you will be living among scorpions. But do not be afraid of what they say, or frightened by the way they look at you. They are people who refuse to obey.

pt.L: E tu, filho do homem, não tenhas medo deles, e não tenhas medo das suas palavras, ainda que sarças e espinhos [estejam] contigo e tu estejas sentado entre escorpiões. Não tenhas medo das suas palavras, e não te assustes com os seus rostos, pois eles [são] uma casa de rebelião.
pt.B: Quanto a ti, filho do homem, não tenhas medo deles nem do que dizem, ainda que espinhos e sarças te rodeiem e tu vivas entre escorpiões. Não tenhas medo das suas palavras nem te assustes com os seus olhares, pois são uma casa rebelde.
pt.R: Mas tu, filho do homem, não deves ter medo deles nem do que eles dizem. Eles vão ser como espinhos e sarças ao teu redor, e tu vais viver no meio de escorpiões. Mas não tenhas medo do que eles dizem, nem te assustes com o jeito como olham para ti. Eles são um povo que se recusa a obedecer.

sw.L: Nawe, mwana wa binadamu, usiwaogope, wala usiyaogope maneno yao, ingawa michongoma na miiba [iko] pamoja nawe, nawe unakaa kati ya nge. Usiyaogope maneno yao, wala usifadhaike kwa nyuso zao, kwa maana wao [ni] nyumba ya uasi.
sw.B: Lakini wewe, mwana wa binadamu, usiwaogope wala usiogope wanayosema, ingawa miiba na michongoma inakuzunguka nawe unaishi kati ya nge. Usiyaogope maneno yao wala usifadhaike kwa jinsi wanavyokutazama, kwa maana wao ni nyumba ya waasi.
sw.R: Lakini wewe, mwana wa binadamu, usiwaogope wala usiogope wanayosema. Watakuwa kama miiba na michongoma inayokuzunguka, nawe utakuwa ukiishi kati ya nge. Usiogope wanayosema wala usitishwe na jinsi wanavyokutazama. Wao ni watu wanaokataa kutii.

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, no tengas miedo de ellos, ni tengas miedo de sus palabras, aunque [haya] zarzas y espinos contigo y estés sentado entre escorpiones. No tengas miedo de sus palabras, ni te espantes ante sus rostros, porque ellos [son] una casa de rebelión.
es.B: Y tú, hijo de hombre, no les tengas miedo ni temas lo que dicen, aunque te rodeen espinos y zarzas y vivas entre escorpiones. No temas sus palabras ni te asustes por sus miradas, porque son una casa rebelde.
es.R: Pero tú, hijo de hombre, no tengas miedo de ellos ni de lo que dicen. Serán como espinos y zarzas a tu alrededor, y vivirás entre escorpiones. Pero no tengas miedo de lo que dicen ni te asustes por la manera en que te miran. Son un pueblo que se niega a obedecer.

vi.L: Và ngươi, hỡi con người, đừng sợ chúng, và đừng sợ lời của chúng, dù gai góc và bụi gai [ở] với ngươi và ngươi đang ngồi giữa bọ cạp. Đừng sợ lời của chúng, và đừng kinh hãi trước mặt chúng, vì chúng [là] nhà của sự phản nghịch.
vi.B: Còn con, hỡi con người, đừng sợ chúng hay sợ những gì chúng nói, dù gai góc và bụi gai vây quanh con và con sống giữa bọ cạp. Đừng sợ lời chúng nói, cũng đừng kinh hãi trước vẻ mặt của chúng, vì chúng là nhà phản nghịch.
vi.R: Nhưng con, hỡi con người, đừng sợ chúng hay sợ những gì chúng nói. Chúng sẽ như gai góc và bụi gai quanh con, và con sẽ sống giữa bọ cạp. Nhưng đừng sợ những gì chúng nói, cũng đừng hoảng sợ vì cách chúng nhìn con. Chúng là dân không chịu vâng lời.

ko.L: 그리고 너, 사람의 아들아, 너는 그들을 두려워하지 말고, 그들의 말도 두려워하지 마라. 가시덤불과 가시가 너와 함께 있고 네가 전갈들 가운데 앉아 있어도, 그들의 말을 두려워하지 말고, 그들의 얼굴 앞에서 떨지 마라. 그들은 반역의 집이다.
ko.B: 너 사람의 아들아, 비록 가시덤불과 가시가 너를 둘러싸고 네가 전갈들 가운데 산다 해도, 너는 그들을 두려워하지 말고 그들이 하는 말도 두려워하지 마라. 그들의 말을 두려워하지 말고, 그들의 얼굴빛에 놀라지 마라. 그들은 반역하는 족속이다.
ko.R: 그러나 너 사람의 아들아, 너는 그들도, 그들이 하는 말도 두려워하지 마라. 그들은 네 둘레의 가시덤불과 가시 같을 것이고, 너는 전갈들 가운데 사는 것 같을 것이다. 그래도 그들이 하는 말을 두려워하지 말고, 그들이 너를 노려보는 눈길에 겁먹지 마라. 그들은 말을 듣지 않는 백성이다.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, n’aie pas peur d’eux, et n’aie pas peur de leurs paroles, même si des ronces et des épines [sont] avec toi et que tu es assis parmi des scorpions. N’aie pas peur de leurs paroles, et ne sois pas effrayé devant leurs faces, car ils [sont] une maison de rébellion.
fr.B: Quant à toi, fils d’homme, ne les crains pas, ne crains pas ce qu’ils disent, même si des épines et des ronces t’entourent et que tu habites parmi des scorpions. Ne crains pas leurs paroles et ne te laisse pas effrayer par leurs regards, car c’est une maison rebelle.
fr.R: Mais toi, fils d’homme, tu ne dois pas avoir peur d’eux ni de ce qu’ils disent. Ils seront comme des épines et des ronces autour de toi, et tu vivras au milieu des scorpions. Mais n’aie pas peur de ce qu’ils disent, et ne te laisse pas effrayer par la façon dont ils te regardent. C’est un peuple qui refuse d’obéir.

decisions.choice: briers and thorns: prickly plants
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain; it is probably a thorny plant, beside a second word for thorns (28:24). Some take it from a word meaning "rebellious", which would make a play on "a house of rebellion".

decisions.choice: thorns and scorpions: the hostility of the people
decisions.reason: The pictures stand for the people Ezekiel will live among: they will wound him with their words and their looks. The LORD does not promise that they will be kind, only that he need not be afraid.

decisions.choice: their looks (B); the way they look at you (R)
decisions.reason: "Their faces" means the hostile looks they will give him. Readable takes the thorns and scorpions as pictures of the people (m2) by saying "They will be like".

decisions.choice: a house of rebellion / a rebellious house / people who refuse to obey
decisions.reason: The wording set at verse 5.

source.text: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֶת־דְּבָרַי֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּ֑לוּ כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you will speak my words to them, whether they will hear or whether they will refrain, for rebellion [are] they.

en.L: And you will speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to them, whether they hear or refrain, for they [are] rebellion.
en.B: You must speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to them, whether they listen or refuse, for they are rebellious.
en.R: You must tell them what I say, whether they listen or not, because they refuse to obey.

pt.L: E tu falarás as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras a eles, quer ouçam, quer deixem de ouvir, pois eles [são] rebelião.
pt.B: Tu deves dizer a eles as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras, quer escutem, quer se recusem, pois são rebeldes.
pt.R: Tu deves dizer a eles o que eu digo, quer escutem, quer não, porque eles se recusam a obedecer.

sw.L: Nawe utawaambia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwamba watasikia au kwamba wataacha, kwa maana wao [ni] uasi.
sw.B: Ni lazima uwaambie maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwamba watasikiliza au watakataa, kwa maana wao ni waasi.
sw.R: Ni lazima uwaambie ninayosema, kwamba watasikiliza au hawatasikiliza, kwa sababu wanakataa kutii.

es.L: Y les hablarás {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, ya sea que escuchen o que dejen de escuchar, porque ellos [son] rebelión.
es.B: Tú les dirás {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, escuchen o se nieguen, porque son rebeldes.
es.R: Tienes que decirles lo que yo digo, escuchen o no, porque se niegan a obedecer.

vi.L: Và ngươi sẽ nói lời của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho chúng, dù chúng nghe hay chúng từ chối, vì chúng [là] sự phản nghịch.
vi.B: Con phải nói lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho chúng, dù chúng nghe hay không chịu nghe, vì chúng là kẻ phản nghịch.
vi.R: Con phải nói cho chúng biết những gì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo con, dù chúng có nghe hay không, vì chúng không chịu vâng lời.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 듣든지 거부하든지, 너는 그들에게 내 말을 전하여라. 그들은 반역이다.
ko.B: 그들이 듣든지 듣기를 거부하든지, 너는 그들에게 내 말을 전해야 한다. 그들은 반역하는 자들이다.
ko.R: 그들이 듣든지 듣지 않든지, 너는 내가 하는 말을 그들에게 전해야 한다. 그들은 말을 듣지 않는 자들이다.

fr.L: Et tu leur diras {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, qu’ils écoutent ou qu’ils s’abstiennent, car ils [sont] rébellion.
fr.B: Tu dois leur dire {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, qu’ils écoutent ou qu’ils refusent, car ils sont rebelles.
fr.R: Tu dois leur dire ce que je dis, qu’ils écoutent ou non, parce qu’ils refusent d’obéir.

decisions.choice: they are rebellion: rebellion itself
alternatives: they are a house of rebellion
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the noun alone: they are rebellion. It is a stronger way of saying "a house of rebellion" (verses 5-6). The Greek translation, and some Hebrew manuscripts, read "a house of rebellion" here as well. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: tell them what I say (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "what I say" for "my words". "They refuse to obey" keeps the Readable wording for this people (verse 5).

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם שְׁמַע֙ אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תְּהִי־מֶ֖רִי כְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑רִי פְּצֵ֣ה פִ֔יךָ וֶאֱכֹ֕ל אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֥ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, hear what I [am] speaking to you; do not be rebellious like the house of the rebellion; open your mouth and eat what I [am] giving to you.

en.L: And you, son of man, hear what I am speaking to you; do not be rebellious like the house of rebellion. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."
en.B: But you, son of man, listen to what I am saying to you. Do not rebel as that rebellious house does. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."
en.R: But you, son of man, must listen to what I tell you. Do not refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as they do. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."

pt.L: E tu, filho do homem, ouve o que eu te falo; não sejas rebelde como a casa de rebelião. Abre a tua boca e come o que eu te dou."
pt.B: Mas tu, filho do homem, escuta o que eu te digo. Não te rebeles como essa casa rebelde. Abre a boca e come o que eu te dou."
pt.R: Mas tu, filho do homem, deves escutar o que eu te digo. Não te recuses a {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} obedecer, como eles fazem. Abre a boca e come o que eu estou te dando."

sw.L: Nawe, mwana wa binadamu, sikia ninayokuambia; usiwe mwasi kama nyumba ya uasi. Fungua kinywa chako ule ninachokupa."
sw.B: Lakini wewe, mwana wa binadamu, sikiliza ninayokuambia. Usiasi kama nyumba ile ya waasi inavyofanya. Fungua kinywa chako ule ninachokupa."
sw.R: Lakini wewe, mwana wa binadamu, ni lazima usikilize ninayokuambia. Usikatae kunitii kama wao wanavyofanya. Fungua kinywa chako ule ninachokupa."

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, oye lo que yo te hablo; no seas rebelde como la casa de rebelión. Abre tu boca y come lo que yo te doy».
es.B: Pero tú, hijo de hombre, escucha lo que te digo. No seas rebelde como esa casa rebelde. Abre la boca y come lo que te doy».
es.R: Pero tú, hijo de hombre, tienes que escuchar lo que te digo. No te rebeles contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como ellos. Abre la boca y come lo que te doy».

vi.L: Và ngươi, hỡi con người, hãy nghe điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang phán với ngươi; đừng phản nghịch như nhà của sự phản nghịch. Hãy mở miệng ngươi ra và ăn điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ban cho ngươi."
vi.B: Nhưng con, hỡi con người, hãy nghe điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang phán với con. Đừng phản nghịch như nhà phản nghịch ấy. Hãy mở miệng ra và ăn điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ban cho con."
vi.R: Nhưng con, hỡi con người, phải lắng nghe điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo con. Đừng bất tuân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như chúng. Hãy mở miệng ra và ăn vật {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ban cho con."

ko.L: 그리고 너, 사람의 아들아, 내가 너에게 하는 말을 들어라. 너는 저 반역의 집처럼 반역하지 마라. 네 입을 벌리고 내가 너에게 주는 것을 먹어라."
ko.B: 그러나 너 사람의 아들아, 내가 너에게 하는 말을 들어라. 너는 저 반역하는 족속처럼 반역하지 마라. 네 입을 벌리고 내가 너에게 주는 것을 먹어라."
ko.R: 그러나 너 사람의 아들아, 내가 너에게 하는 말을 잘 들어라. 너는 그들처럼 내 말을 거역하지 마라. 입을 벌리고 내가 주는 것을 먹어라."

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, écoute ce que je te dis ; ne sois pas rebelle comme la maison de rébellion. Ouvre ta bouche et mange ce que je te donne. »
fr.B: Mais toi, fils d’homme, écoute ce que je te dis. Ne te rebelle pas comme cette maison rebelle. Ouvre la bouche et mange ce que je te donne. »
fr.R: Mais toi, fils d’homme, tu dois écouter ce que je te dis. Ne refuse pas de {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}obéir comme eux. Ouvre la bouche et mange ce que je te donne. »

decisions.choice: do not be rebellious like the house of rebellion: the prophet must obey first
decisions.reason: Ezekiel can only call the people to obey if he obeys himself. His first test is a strange command: to eat what he is given, before he knows what it is.

decisions.choice: open your mouth and eat: taking in God's word
decisions.reason: Jeremiah says, "Your words were found, and I ate them" (Jeremiah 15:16). What Ezekiel is given to eat is shown in verse 9: a scroll. The scene goes on in 3:1-3.

decisions.choice: Do not refuse to obey me as they do (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses its wording for "a house of rebellion" and says "as they do" for "like the house of rebellion". "Me" here is the LORD speaking of himself; Readable adds it to make plain whom Ezekiel must not refuse, as the context implies. The quotation mark closes the speech begun in verse 3.

source.text: וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה־יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה־ב֖וֹ מְגִלַּת־סֵֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I looked, and see, a hand stretched out to me, and see, in it a scroll of a book.

en.L: And I looked, and see, a hand [was] stretched out to me, and see, in it [was] the scroll of a book.
en.B: Then I looked, and I saw a hand stretched out toward me, and in it was a written scroll.
en.R: Then I saw a hand reaching out to me. It was holding a scroll with writing on it.

pt.L: E olhei, e eis que uma mão [estava] estendida para mim, e eis que nela [havia] o rolo de um livro.
pt.B: Então olhei e vi uma mão estendida para mim, e nela havia um rolo escrito.
pt.R: Então vi uma mão que se estendia para mim. Ela segurava um rolo com coisas escritas.

sw.L: Nikatazama, na tazama, mkono [ulikuwa] umenyooshwa kwangu, na tazama, ndani yake [lilikuwa] gombo la kitabu.
sw.B: Kisha nikatazama, nikaona mkono umenyooshwa kuelekea kwangu, na ndani yake kulikuwa na gombo lililoandikwa.
sw.R: Kisha nikaona mkono ukinyooshwa kunielekea. Ulikuwa umeshika gombo lililoandikwa maneno.

es.L: Y miré, y he aquí, una mano [estaba] extendida hacia mí, y he aquí, en ella [había] un rollo de libro.
es.B: Entonces miré y vi una mano extendida hacia mí, y en ella había un rollo escrito.
es.R: Entonces vi una mano que se extendía hacia mí. Sostenía un rollo con algo escrito.

vi.L: Và tôi nhìn, và kìa, một bàn tay đưa ra về phía tôi, và kìa, trong tay ấy [có] một cuộn sách.
vi.B: Bấy giờ tôi nhìn và thấy một bàn tay đưa về phía tôi, trong tay có một cuộn sách đã viết chữ.
vi.R: Rồi tôi thấy một bàn tay đưa ra về phía tôi. Bàn tay ấy cầm một cuộn sách có viết chữ.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 보니, 보라, 손 하나가 나에게 뻗쳐 있었고, 보라, 그 손에 두루마리 책이 [있었다].
ko.B: 그때 내가 보니, 손 하나가 나를 향해 뻗쳐 있었고, 그 손에는 글이 적힌 두루마리가 들려 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 손 하나가 나에게 뻗쳐 오는 것이 보였다. 그 손에는 글이 적힌 두루마리가 들려 있었다.

fr.L: Et je regardai, et voici, une main [était] tendue vers moi, et voici, en elle [était] un rouleau de livre.
fr.B: Alors je regardai, et je vis une main tendue vers moi ; elle tenait un rouleau écrit.
fr.R: Alors j’ai vu une main qui se tendait vers moi. Elle tenait un rouleau avec quelque chose d’écrit dessus.

decisions.choice: the scroll of a book: a written scroll
decisions.reason: Books were written on long strips of leather or papyrus and rolled up. The phrase "scroll of a book" is also used of the scroll Jeremiah dictated to Baruch (Jeremiah 36:2). The hand is not said to be anyone's; the vision lets it stand for the LORD's giving.

decisions.choice: see (L)
decisions.reason: The pointing word, traditionally "behold", is "see" at Literal, as in 1:4; Balanced and Readable fold it into "I saw".

decisions.choice: gombo
decisions.reason: A scroll is "gombo", as in the published Luke 4:17 and Jeremiah 36; "kitabu" alone would suggest a bound book. Literal adds "la kitabu" for the Hebrew "scroll of a book".

decisions.choice: "un rollo de libro"
decisions.reason: As Jeremiah 36:2 L in Spanish

decisions.choice: "두루마리 책" (L); "글이 적힌 두루마리" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the scroll, as Jeremiah 36 and Hebrews 10:7.

decisions.choice: "un rouleau de livre" (Literal); "un rouleau écrit" (Balanced); "un rouleau avec quelque chose d'écrit dessus" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Rouleau de livre" at Literal as in the published Jeremiah; a book was a scroll, so Balanced and Readable say what it was.

decisions.choice: o rolo de um livro (L); um rolo escrito (B); um rolo com coisas escritas (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (2:9-3:3): the scroll (m1) is "rolo" at every level, the word Jeremiah 36:2 and Revelation 10:9-10 use in Portuguese, so that the scroll Ezekiel eats is the same word as the one John eats. Literal keeps "rolo de livro" as Jeremiah 36:2 does; "livro" alone would make readers think of bound pages.

source.text: וַיִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אוֹתָהּ֙ לְפָנַ֔י וְהִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה פָּנִ֣ים וְאָח֑וֹר וְכָת֣וּב אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he spread it before me, and it [was] written front and back, and [there were] written on it laments and moaning and woe.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spread it out before me, and it [was] written on the front and on the back, and written on it [were] laments and mourning and woe.
en.B: He unrolled it in front of me, and it had writing on the front and on the back. Written on it were laments and mourning and woe.
en.R: He opened it up in front of me. There was writing on both sides. It was full of funeral songs, sad cries and words of woe.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} o estendeu diante de mim, e ele [estava] escrito na frente e no verso, e escritos nele [estavam] lamentos, e gemidos, e ais.
pt.B: Ele o desenrolou diante de mim, e estava escrito na frente e no verso. Nele estavam escritos lamentos, gemidos e ais.
pt.R: Ele o abriu na minha frente. Havia coisas escritas dos dois lados. O rolo estava cheio de cantos fúnebres, gritos de tristeza e palavras de desgraça.

sw.L: Naye akalikunjua mbele yangu, nalo [lilikuwa] limeandikwa mbele na nyuma, na yaliyoandikwa juu yake [yalikuwa] maombolezo na kilio na ole.
sw.B: Akalikunjua mbele yangu, nalo lilikuwa limeandikwa mbele na nyuma. Yaliyoandikwa juu yake yalikuwa maombolezo, kilio na ole.
sw.R: Akalifungua mbele yangu. Lilikuwa limeandikwa pande zote mbili. Lilijaa nyimbo za mazishi, vilio vya huzuni na maneno ya ole.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo desplegó delante de mí, y estaba escrito por delante y por detrás, y escritos en él [había] lamentos y gemidos y ayes.
es.B: Lo desenrolló delante de mí, y tenía escritura por delante y por detrás. En él estaban escritos lamentos, gemidos y ayes.
es.R: Lo abrió delante de mí. Estaba escrito por los dos lados. Estaba lleno de cantos fúnebres, gritos de tristeza y palabras de dolor.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trải nó ra trước mặt tôi, và nó [được] viết cả mặt trước lẫn mặt sau, và trên đó có viết những bài ai ca, tiếng than thở và lời khốn thay.
vi.B: Ngài mở cuộn sách ra trước mặt tôi; cuộn sách có viết chữ cả mặt trước lẫn mặt sau. Trên đó có viết những lời ai ca, than khóc và khốn khổ.
vi.R: Ngài mở cuộn sách ra trước mặt tôi. Cả hai mặt đều có viết chữ. Cuộn sách đầy những bài ca tang chế, những tiếng kêu than và những lời than van về tai họa.

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 그것을 내 앞에 펼치셨는데, 그것은 앞뒤로 글이 적혀 있었고, 그 위에는 애가와 탄식과 재앙의 말이 적혀 있었다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 앞에서 그것을 펼치셨는데, 앞뒤에 글이 적혀 있었다. 거기에는 애가와 탄식과 재앙의 말이 적혀 있었다.
ko.R: 그분께서 내 앞에서 그것을 펴 보이셨다. 두루마리 양면에 글이 가득 적혀 있었다. 거기에는 장례 노래와 슬피 우는 소리와 재앙을 알리는 말이 가득했다.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le déroula devant moi, et il [était] écrit devant et derrière, et sur lui [étaient] écrits des complaintes, et des gémissements, et des malheurs.
fr.B: Il le déroula devant moi : le rouleau était écrit au recto et au verso. On y avait écrit des complaintes, des gémissements et des cris de malheur.
fr.R: Il a déroulé le rouleau devant moi. Le rouleau était écrit des deux côtés. Il était rempli de chants de deuil, de cris de tristesse et de paroles de malheur.

decisions.choice: written on the front and on the back: a scroll with no room for more
decisions.reason: Scrolls were usually written on the inner side only. This one is full on both sides, so that nothing can be added: the message is complete. Revelation 5:1 takes up the picture of a scroll "written inside and on the back".

decisions.choice: laments and mourning and woe: the message is grief
decisions.reason: The first word is the funeral song, the lament for the dead (19:1; 27:2; 2 Samuel 1:17); the second means moaning; the third, which occurs only here, is a cry of woe. Before Ezekiel speaks of hope (chapters 33-48), he must announce the death of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: He unrolled it (B); He opened it up (R)
decisions.reason: To spread out a scroll is to unroll it so that it can be read. The pronoun for God at the start of a sentence is capitalized under either setting. Readable says "funeral songs" for laments (m2).

decisions.choice: "complaintes" (Literal, Balanced); "chants de deuil" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for qinah, used again for the laments of chapters 19, 26-28 and 32.
